Speaker: Nema, Founder of Salt and Stone (Body care brand, deodorants, sunscreen, body wash).
Scale: $165M+ revenue. Rumored $500M+ exit. Two private equity transactions (Humble Growth and Advent). Best-selling deodorant on Amazon, Sephora, Erewhon. Sells one deodorant every 5 seconds.
Brand/Product strategy (BRD / PRD):
Started with sunscreen, but deodorant became the hero product.
Wanted to bring "design" to a boring category. Beautiful packaging to leave on the counter, not hide in a drawer. High price point aligns with premium design.
Scent innovation: Deodorant should smell like sophisticated perfume, not just peppermint or lavender. Used "Noses" (perfumers) but relied on a tight inner circle of taste-makers for final approval.
Product development took years, 8 generations of formulas for the deodorant.
Refused to launch exclusively in Sephora; it's an "everybody brand" across multiple channels.
COGS/Supplier (COG):
Found manufacturers by looking at who makes for big brands (like Oakley).

Mistake: Trusting a contract manufacturer without fully vetting capacity and certifications. Big brands vet them out, small brands sometimes rush. Need around 10 different contract manufacturers now for scale.
Wild Bets / Collaborations (WLD):
Collaborations with Brain Dead, Stussy, Outdoor Voices, Aritzia, Kendall Jenner's 818, Erewhon smoothies, Alaska Airlines.
Not driven by profit; driven by "noise" and fun.
Create custom fragrances for collaborations (e.g., "Lily and Yuzu" for Aritzia).
Finance & Accounting / Exits (FIN):
Profitable since day 1. Cash collected as soon as product ships.
Took chips off the table via Private Equity (Humble Growth and Advent) while maintaining control.
Diluted equity without taking cash to the balance sheet (secondary transaction).
Humble Growth: Chosen because they were former founders (Andrew Abraham of Orgain). Let Nema run the business.
Advent: Chosen for the long-term vision (to be like Nike).
Advised founders looking for a full exit to not attend the PE meetings, as buyers will want the founder to stay if they think the founder is the magic.
Leadership/Team (OPX/Team?):
100% remote company.
Looks for "mini-CEOs" who don't separate work/life balance, self-starters.
Doesn't do many formal 1-on-1s. Constantly communicating via text/calls.
Hires via LinkedIn scouting (spent hours acting as GM).
Uses 4 years of customer service experience to read reviews directly. Still reads every review that comes to his inbox.
Ecommerce/Retail (SET / GAD? No, just retail strategy):
80% DTC, 20% wholesale.
Amazon strategy: Got the #1 bestseller badge before even advertising.
